title: 2026-10-22_Linux_P2P_Ransom_Botnet_Investigation_213
description: Investigate and respond to a Linux P2P Ransom botnet malware incident.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents. Your task is to investigate and respond to these incidents.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim machine with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that is periodically communicating with an external host?
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services. The suspicious service is likely named `bot-beacon.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that might be responsible for network communication.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl status bot-beacon.service` to check the status of the service.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Network Traffic Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service generating abnormal volumes of network traffic?
levels.solution: Investigate the systemd services and look for any services that might be responsible for network flooding. The service is likely named `bot-flood.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate the systemd services and look for any services that might be responsible for network flooding.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that might be generating high volumes of network traffic.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl status bot-flood.service` to check the status of the service.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service?
levels.solution: Examine the systemd timers and services to understand how the service maintains persistence. The persistence mechanism is likely a systemd timer named `bot-beacon.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd timers and services to understand how the service maintains persistence.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers that might be responsible for starting the service periodically.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl status bot-beacon.timer` to check the status of the timer.
